newsitem.title: USA: USDA eases rules for transgenic field tests.
newsitem.headline: USDA eases rules for transgenic field tests.

text.p: The Agriculture Department on Friday said it would simplify its rules for researchers introducing certain kinds of genetically-engineered plants and products derived from known plant pests.

In a notice published in the Federal Register, the USDA said the changes would also simplify the requirements for determination of non-regulated status, and for procedures for reporting field tests of genetically-engineered plants.

The changes would let the agency's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service extend an existing determination of non-regulated status to other things that are "closely related" to the first organism.
The USDA said it would also reduce the field test reporting requirements for some trials conducted under permits.
The rules become effective on June 2, the agency said.

"The agricultural biotechnology industry is still in a relatively early stage of development," USDA said. "Each year, as the industry continues to grow, it is anticipated there will be growth in experimentation, ultimately resulting in an increase in agricultural production and a broadening of international trade. The potential benefits could be significant, but are speculative at this time."

Currently, some 85 percent of all field trials must be conducted under the USDA's existing notification procedures. The rule changes mean that less than 0.5 percent of the transgenic plants field tested will be exempt from the notification procedures, the agency said.
